question: Should `/v1/chat/completions` expose internal OpenClaw agent tool calls at all, and if so what opt-in, authorization, redaction, and response-shape contract should gate it?
rationale: Source and docs show this would expand the public Gateway API beyond caller-supplied tools and could reveal sensitive operator context, so automation should not choose the product/security boundary.

options.title: Keep client-tool-only contract
options.body: Leave Chat Completions `tool_calls` limited to caller-supplied tools and direct internal-tool observability to a separate Gateway trace or diagnostic surface.

options.title: Design opt-in telemetry mode
options.body: Add a maintainer-approved default-off mode with redaction, scopes, docs, and tests before exposing internal tool names or arguments through HTTP.

options.title: Reopen a canonical Responses trace design
options.body: Use the prior OpenResponses audit discussion as the canonical place for internal tool visibility and keep this Chat Completions request blocked until that shape is settled.

recommendation.title: Keep client-tool-only contract
recommendation.body: Leave Chat Completions `tool_calls` limited to caller-supplied tools and direct internal-tool observability to a separate Gateway trace or diagnostic surface.

likelyOwner.reason: The original Gateway HTTP API and adjacent security/gateway refactor history make this the best available owner signal for a boundary decision.
